Read cache

Run the cache

isledb cache is the regional read cache as a service. It relays CURRENT for each database it serves, reading it from storage every 500 ms, and serves immutable objects from 128 KiB chunks on local disk. The HTTP API is in read-cache-api.md.

isledb cache --config /etc/isledb/isledb.yaml

or, without a file:

isledb cache \
  --bucket-url 's3://my-bucket?region=us-east-1' \
  --db prod/policy --db prod/flags \
  --disk-dir /var/cache/isledb --disk-bytes 200GiB \
  --auth-token-file /etc/isledb/tokens

Storage credentials come from the provider's usual environment (for S3, the AWS SDK chain: environment variables, shared config, instance or pod role). They are never set in the cache's own configuration.

Configuration

Each setting can come from the YAML file, an environment variable or a flag. A flag overrides the environment, the environment overrides the file, and the file overrides the default. --db on the command line, or ISLEDB_CACHE_DATABASES, replaces the file's list of databases rather than adding to it.

One file can configure every isledb role: settings all roles share sit at the top, and each role reads its own section. The cache reads cache:.

bucket_url: s3://my-bucket?region=us-east-1
log_level: info

cache:
  listen: :8090
  admin_listen: 127.0.0.1:8091

  disk:
    dir: /var/cache/isledb
    bytes: 200GiB

  reads:
    max_bytes: 256MiB
    max_wait: 5s

  current:
    poll: 500ms
    long_poll: 30s

  databases:
    - prefix: prod/policy
    - prefix: prod/flags
      current_poll: 250ms

  auth:
    token_file: /etc/isledb/tokens

  tls:
    cert: /etc/isledb/tls/cert.pem
    key: /etc/isledb/tls/key.pem
    client_ca: /etc/isledb/tls/clients.pem

  shutdown_drain: 5s

Unknown keys are an error, at the top and inside cache:, so a misspelled key stops the cache at start rather than being ignored. Sections of the other roles this binary has are left for them; a section named after no role is an error too. The file holds paths, never secrets: tokens and keys stay in their own files.

A database at the root of the bucket is written /. An empty prefix is an error, so a blank value never names the root, and so is one with an empty, . or .. segment (prod//a, prod/../a), whose keys would never match.

isledb cache --config isledb.yaml --check validates the configuration, prints it as resolved from every source, and exits.

Naming. A setting's environment variable is ISLEDB_ followed by its key, upper case with dots as underscores: the shared settings as they are (bucket_url → ISLEDB_BUCKET_URL), the cache's after CACHE_ (cache.disk.bytes → ISLEDB_CACHE_DISK_BYTES). An environment variable set to an empty value counts: ISLEDB_CACHE_ADMIN_LISTEN= turns the admin listener off.

File key Flag Environment Default
bucket_url --bucket-url ISLEDB_BUCKET_URL required Bucket holding the databases
log_level --log-level ISLEDB_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warn, error
cache.databases[].prefix --db (repeat) ISLEDB_CACHE_DATABASES (comma-separated) required Databases served, by prefix; / for the bucket root
cache.databases[].current_poll – – cache.current.poll Per-database poll interval
cache.listen --listen ISLEDB_CACHE_LISTEN :8090 API address
cache.admin_listen --admin-listen ISLEDB_CACHE_ADMIN_LISTEN 127.0.0.1:8091 Admin address; empty for none
cache.disk.dir --disk-dir ISLEDB_CACHE_DISK_DIR required Chunk directory, on local disk
cache.disk.bytes --disk-bytes ISLEDB_CACHE_DISK_BYTES required Disk budget
cache.reads.max_bytes --max-read-bytes ISLEDB_CACHE_READS_MAX_BYTES 256MiB Bytes read from storage at once; at least 4MiB
cache.reads.max_wait --max-read-wait ISLEDB_CACHE_READS_MAX_WAIT 5s Longest a storage read waits for budget. About half the readers' timeout to the cache.
cache.current.poll --current-poll ISLEDB_CACHE_CURRENT_POLL 500ms How often CURRENT is read
cache.current.long_poll --long-poll ISLEDB_CACHE_CURRENT_LONG_POLL 30s Longest a long poll is held, at most 30s
cache.auth.token_file --auth-token-file ISLEDB_CACHE_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE Bearer tokens, one per line
cache.auth.insecure --insecure ISLEDB_CACHE_AUTH_INSECURE false No authentication, for development
cache.tls.cert, cache.tls.key --tls-cert, --tls-key ISLEDB_CACHE_TLS_CERT, ISLEDB_CACHE_TLS_KEY Serve TLS
cache.tls.client_ca --tls-client-ca ISLEDB_CACHE_TLS_CLIENT_CA Require client certificates signed by this CA
cache.shutdown_drain --shutdown-drain ISLEDB_CACHE_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN 5s Not-ready time before shutting down
– --config ISLEDB_CONFIG YAML file

Sizes are bytes or binary units: 512KiB, 256MiB, 200GiB, 2TiB. Durations are Go durations: 250ms, 30s, 2m.

Authentication

The cache refuses to start without authentication unless cache.auth.insecure is set.

  • Tokens. cache.auth.token_file holds one token per line; blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped. Clients send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Send SIGHUP to reread the file; if the new file cannot be read or holds no tokens, the tokens in use stay.
  • Client certificates. With cache.tls.client_ca, clients must present a certificate it signed. With both tokens and client certificates set, both are required. An isledb reader presents one with read_cache.cert and read_cache.key, and trusts a cache certificate from a private CA with read_cache.ca_file.

Each database is served only its own objects: those right under its prefix, not those of a database nested under it (prod/a/b under prod/a), and, for the root, not those of the databases under prefixes. A client can read through the cache only the databases it is configured to serve.

Admin endpoints

On admin_listen, without authentication; keep it on an address only operators and scrapers reach.

Path
/healthz 200 while the process runs
/readyz 200 once every database's CURRENT has been read once; 503 before, and while shutting down. It stays 200 while storage is down: the cache keeps serving its copy, and readers judge its age.
/metrics Prometheus
/debug/pprof/ Go profiles

Metrics

Metric
isledb_cache_chunks_total{source} Chunks served: disk, storage, shared, bridged
isledb_cache_object_responses_total{status} Object responses by Isledb-Cache: hit, shared, miss
isledb_cache_storage_reads_total, isledb_cache_storage_read_bytes_total Storage range reads and bytes
isledb_cache_storage_reads_queued_total Storage reads that waited for cache.reads.max_bytes
isledb_cache_storage_bytes_reading Bytes being read now
isledb_cache_size_lookups_total Sizes asked of storage, for requests without Isledb-Object-Size
isledb_cache_current_position{db}, isledb_cache_current_age_seconds{db} The relayed CURRENT
isledb_cache_current_poll_errors_total{db} Failed reads of CURRENT
isledb_cache_long_polls_held Long polls waiting now
isledb_cache_disk_bytes, isledb_cache_disk_max_bytes, isledb_cache_disk_entries, isledb_cache_disk_evictions_total, isledb_cache_disk_failures_total The chunk store
isledb_cache_http_requests_total{route,code}, isledb_cache_http_request_seconds{route} Requests; route is current, current_long_poll, object or other

What to watch:

  • current_age_seconds rising means storage is not answering; readers stop accepting the copy once it is older than their age limit.
  • storage_reads_queued_total rising means reads wait for budget: raise cache.reads.max_bytes, or add replicas, before waits reach cache.reads.max_wait and turn into 502s.
  • disk_evictions_total rising fast with a low hit share means the disk is too small for the working set.

Shutdown

On SIGTERM or SIGINT the cache:

  1. reports not ready on /readyz;
  2. waits cache.shutdown_drain for load balancers to notice;
  3. answers every held long poll with the position it has;
  4. finishes requests in flight, for up to 30 seconds, and exits.

A second SIGTERM or SIGINT during these steps ends the process at once.

Chunks on disk are kept. After a restart, requests carrying Isledb-Object-Size are served from them at once.

Deploying

  • Disk. Put cache.disk.dir on local SSD. One process per directory: the chunk store locks it.
  • Timeouts in front of the cache. Load balancers and proxies must allow idle connections longer than cache.current.long_poll, or they cut long polls off. An isledb reader waits up to 10 seconds for the cache, then reads storage itself. cache.reads.max_wait, 5 seconds by default, is about half that, so a read that waited for its turn still has time to fetch and answer. Raise it only for clients that wait longer, to about half their timeout.
  • Several replicas. Round-robin works: each replica relays CURRENT on its own, and readers treat a copy behind their view as nothing new. Each replica then caches every hot chunk. Hashing object requests by path at the load balancer (Envoy ring hash, NGINX hash $uri consistent) puts each chunk on one replica, so their disks add up instead of repeating each other. /v1/current can stay round-robin.
  • Readiness. Route traffic by /readyz, not /healthz.

Kubernetes

The admin address defaults to 127.0.0.1:8091, which the kubelet's probes cannot reach from outside the container. Bind it to all interfaces in the pod, and keep it off the Service.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: isledb-cache
spec:
  serviceName: isledb-cache
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: isledb-cache }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: isledb-cache }
    spec:
      # Longer than cache.shutdown_drain (5s) plus the 30s given to
      # requests in flight.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      containers:
        - name: cache
          image: isledb:latest
          args: ["cache", "--config", "/etc/isledb/isledb.yaml"]
          env:
            - name: ISLEDB_CACHE_ADMIN_LISTEN
              value: "0.0.0.0:8091"
          ports:
            - { name: api, containerPort: 8090 }
            - { name: admin, containerPort: 8091 }
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /readyz, port: admin }
            periodSeconds: 2
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: admin }
            periodSeconds: 10
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: config, mountPath: /etc/isledb, readOnly: true }
            - { name: chunks, mountPath: /var/cache/isledb }
      volumes:
        - name: config
          projected:
            sources:
              - configMap: { name: isledb-config }   # isledb.yaml
              - secret: { name: isledb-tokens }      # tokens
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata: { name: chunks }
      spec:
        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
        storageClassName: local-ssd
        resources: { requests: { storage: 200Gi } }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: isledb-cache
spec:
  selector: { app: isledb-cache }
  ports:
    - { name: api, port: 8090, targetPort: api }   # the admin port is not here
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: isledb-cache-admin
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: { app: isledb-cache }
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - ports: [{ port: 8090 }]                 # the API, from anywhere it is routed
    - ports: [{ port: 8091 }]                 # the admin port, from monitoring only
      from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring }
  • Why a StatefulSet. Each replica keeps its own chunk volume across restarts, so a restarted pod serves hits from disk at once.
  • Probes. Readiness uses /readyz, so a pod takes traffic only once it has read CURRENT for every database; liveness uses /healthz, which does not depend on storage, so a storage outage never restarts the pods. Kubelet probes come from the node, which most network plugins let through regardless of policy; if yours does not, allow the node's addresses on port 8091.
  • Admin port. Not in the Service, and only the monitoring namespace may reach it: it serves /debug/pprof. Scrape /metrics through the pod's admin port.
  • Shutdown. The cache drains on its own: on SIGTERM it reports not ready, waits cache.shutdown_drain, then answers held long polls. No preStop hook is needed.
  • Mixed versions. A pod whose binary lacks a role named in a shared isledb.yaml refuses to start, so roll the image before adding a new role's section to the shared file.

Cache HTTP API

The read cache sits between IsleDB readers in one region and object storage. It serves two things:

  • CURRENT, the one mutable object, relayed from a single copy the cache reads from storage every 500 ms.
  • Immutable objects (SSTs, change batches, manifest pages and snapshots), by byte range, from 128 KiB chunks kept on the cache's disk.

Running it: isledb-cache.md.

Version: v1. Every path starts with /v1/.

Endpoints

Method and path Serves
GET /v1/current?db=P The cache's copy of database P's CURRENT
GET /v1/current?db=P&after=N Its position only, once it passes N (long poll)
GET /v1/object/{key} Bytes of an immutable object, whole or by range

P is a database's prefix in the bucket, as configured on the cache, and / for a database at the bucket root. db may be left out when the cache serves one database.

{key} is the object's full storage key, including the database prefix, exactly as the reader's store names it, for example db/sstable/a3f/000123.sst. Only objects of a database the cache serves are answered (see below).

Authentication

Every request to these endpoints carries Authorization: Bearer <token>, or comes over TLS with a client certificate, as the cache is configured. A request without valid credentials answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.

GET /v1/current

Returns the cache's copy of CURRENT, or, as a long poll, only its position once it passes a given one. A long poll is a doorbell: a reader that sees a new position reads CURRENT with a plain GET /v1/current, so CURRENT reaches readers by one path, where the client rules below apply.

Log position. The position is CURRENT's next_seq: the sequence number the next manifest log entry will get. Every entry appended to the manifest log raises it by one, in the same conditional write of CURRENT that adds the entry. Entries record changes to the database's structure: a flush adding an SST (with its change batch), a compaction, SSTs removed, a checkpoint, or a writer or compactor taking ownership. User writes do not move it until a flush. It never goes down. Some rewrites of CURRENT add no entry and keep the position, such as folding the log into a new snapshot.

Query

Parameter Meaning
after=N Optional. Long poll: hold the request until the copy's log position is above N, or until the server's long-poll timeout, at most 30 seconds, then answer with the position only. N is a log position.

Response headers

Header Without after With after
Isledb-Position Log position of the CURRENT returned: its next_seq The copy's log position
Isledb-Age-Ms Milliseconds since the cache read this CURRENT from storage, rounded up. Measured on the cache's monotonic clock; not a timestamp. The copy's age, the same way
Content-Type application/json –

Without after, the body is CURRENT's bytes as stored. With after, the body is empty.

Status

Status When
200 The copy, with position and age; or, for a long poll, the position. A long poll that timed out also answers 200, with a position not above N.
400 after is not a number, or db is missing on a cache serving several databases
401 No valid credentials
404 db names a database the cache does not serve
503 The cache has not read CURRENT once yet; a long poll gets it at once, not after the timeout

Behaviour

  • The copy never moves back. A CURRENT in storage at a lower position is refused and logged; a store recreated under the same prefix needs the cache restarted.
  • A CURRENT at the same position with other bytes, such as one rewritten around a new snapshot, replaces the copy. It does not answer long polls, which wait for a higher position; the next request gets the new bytes.
  • When storage cannot be read, the cache keeps serving its copy, and its age grows. Readers decide whether it is still young enough.

Client rules (enforced by the reader, so a faulty cache cannot break it)

  1. Age limit. Reject a CURRENT whose age is above 5 seconds and read storage directly.
  2. Load time = the time the request was sent (own clock) − the age. This is when the view's MaxPinnedViewAge starts.
  3. Older means read storage. A CURRENT from the cache at a position below the reader's published view, as a lagging replica can give, is not replayed: the refresh reads CURRENT from storage instead, which also renews the view.
  4. Refresh reads storage directly. The relay can be up to one poll interval behind.
  5. Long poll. Ask with after=<published position>; on an answer above it, call RequestRefresh and ask again. RequestRefresh reads CURRENT with a plain GET, where rules 1 to 3 apply. Give up on a long poll unanswered after 45 seconds: the connection is dead. An answer not above it whose age is past the limit of rule 1 means the cache cannot read storage and will not ring for new commits: read CURRENT, which then goes to storage. After a timeout or error, wait a random 0 to 1 second before asking again.
  6. Fallback. On a connection error, a timeout or a 5xx, read storage directly.

Example

$ curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://cache:8090/v1/current?db=prod/policy&after=41'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Isledb-Age-Ms: 3
Isledb-Position: 42
Content-Length: 0

$ curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://cache:8090/v1/current?db=prod/policy'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Isledb-Age-Ms: 212
Isledb-Position: 42

{"layout_version":…,"next_seq":42,…}

GET /v1/object/{key}

Returns bytes of an immutable object.

Keys served. Only objects that are never rewritten, each a fixed shape right after its database's prefix P (nothing before the shape for the root):

Object Key
SST P/sstable/{bucket}/{id}, where {bucket} is the one id maps to
Change batch P/changes/{bucket}/{id}, same rule
Manifest snapshot P/manifest/snapshots/{name}.manifest.zst
Manifest page P/manifest/pages/l{NN}/{name}.page.zst

A key is answered only when what comes before its shape is exactly a database the cache serves. So each database is served only its own objects: serving prod/a does not serve prod/a/b/sstable/… of a database nested under it, and serving the root does not serve prod/a/sstable/…. Anything else, including manifest/CURRENT and maintenance/HEAD, answers 403.

Request headers

Header Meaning
Range Optional. One range: bytes=a-b, bytes=a- or bytes=-n. Without it, the whole object. Several ranges in one header are refused (416).
Isledb-Object-Size Optional. The object's size in bytes, its full stored length, at most 5 TiB. With it, the cache does not ask storage for the size. IsleDB readers always send it.
Isledb-No-Cache Optional, any value. Serve the bytes without keeping what is read from storage. Chunks already on disk are still used. For scans.

Response headers

Header Meaning
Content-Range On 206: bytes a-b/size. On 416: bytes */size.
Content-Length Bytes in the body
Isledb-Error On an error response, its kind where the status alone does not say: size-mismatch on a 400
Isledb-Cache How the first 4 MiB of the response were served: hit (all from disk), shared (read from storage by another request in flight, none by this one), miss (this request read from storage)
Accept-Ranges bytes
Content-Type application/octet-stream

Status

Status When Client should
200 Whole object Use it
206 The range asked for Use it
400 Isledb-Object-Size is not a positive number up to 5 TiB, or is not the object's size in storage; the latter carries Isledb-Error: size-mismatch Read storage directly; report a bug
401 No valid credentials Fix the token or certificate; read storage directly meanwhile
403 Not an immutable object of a database the cache serves Read storage directly; report a bug
404 The object is not in storage Retry storage directly once, then report not found
405 HEAD request; only GET is served (Allow: GET) Use GET
416 Range outside the object, or several ranges Report a bug
502 Storage failed Read storage directly
other 5xx, connection error, timeout The cache is unhealthy Read storage directly

A 404 is retried against storage because a cache pointed at the wrong bucket or prefix would answer 404 for everything; readers must not trust it alone.

The size

  • The size must be the object's full stored length. For an SST with a Bloom sidecar that is BloomOffset + BloomLength + 16: the sidecar follows the SST's Size, and a 16-byte trailer follows the sidecar. Without one, it is Size. For a change batch it is the batch's Size.
  • Chunks are kept per key and size. A request with a wrong size never reads or replaces chunks kept for the right one.
  • Every read from storage checks the size against the size storage reports, at no extra request. A wrong size is refused (400) and nothing is kept, so only bytes read under the right size are ever served from disk.
  • Without the header the cache asks storage once (a HEAD) and remembers the size in memory until restart.
  • A wrong size larger than the object can instead fail at storage, which refuses a range past the end; the cache then answers 502.

Behaviour

  • Objects are kept as 128 KiB chunks, aligned at offset 0, the same size as the reader's own chunks. The last chunk is shorter.
  • Missing chunks next to each other are read from storage in one request, up to 32 chunks (4 MiB). A request also reads again up to 8 chunks it already has, to join two missing runs into one request.
  • Concurrent requests for the same missing chunk share one storage read.
  • A storage read is not tied to the request that started it: a client that disconnects does not fail others waiting on the same chunks.
  • Storage reads in progress are capped in bytes (MaxReadBytes, default 256 MiB). Past the cap, a read waits its turn, in arrival order, for at most MaxReadWait (default 5 seconds), and then fails with 502. The wait does not shorten the storage request's own 30-second timeout. Set MaxReadWait to about half the readers' timeout to the cache (10 seconds by default), so a read that gets its turn still has time to fetch and answer: a queued read keeps its place after its reader gives up, so a longer wait spends budget on fetches whose requesters have left, ahead of requests still waiting. Hits are never queued.
  • A response is sent 4 MiB at a time. The status and headers are sent once the first 4 MiB are in hand, so an error there gets its own status. A failure after that ends the body early; the client sees fewer bytes than Content-Length.
  • The cache does not check object contents. Readers verify every object as they do when reading storage directly (SST, Bloom, page, snapshot and change-index checksums, and Pebble block checksums).

Examples

A lookup's chunk, cold and then warm:

$ curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://cache:8090/v1/object/db/sstable/a3f/000123.sst \
    -H 'Range: bytes=131072-262143' -H 'Isledb-Object-Size: 8421376'
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Range: bytes 131072-262143/8421376
Content-Length: 131072
Isledb-Cache: miss
…

The next request for that chunk answers Isledb-Cache: hit.

A manifest page, whole:

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://cache:8090/v1/object/db/manifest/pages/l00/p17.page.zst \
    -H 'Isledb-Object-Size: 20381' -o p17.page.zst

A scan that should not fill the cache:

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://cache:8090/v1/object/db/sstable/a3f/000123.sst \
    -H 'Range: bytes=0-4194303' -H 'Isledb-Object-Size: 8421376' \
    -H 'Isledb-No-Cache: 1'

Reader support

Readers configured with a read cache read SSTs, manifest pages and snapshots through it, with fallback to storage, and refresh through the relay with the client rules above and the long poll. Change readers configured with a read cache read change batch indexes and blocks, the feed's view and its manifest pages through it, with the same rules and fallback, and wait for changes with the long poll.
